title: LORA: LOW-RANK ADAPTATION OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
methodology: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices in parallel to existing weight matrices (specifically applied to Wq and Wv in the self-attention module). This approach is compared against Full Fine-tuning (FT) and Adapter-based methods (such as AdapterH and AdapterL).
key_findings: LoRA drastically reduces the number of trainable parameters compared to Full Fine-tuning. For GPT-3 175B, Full Fine-tuning requires 175,255.8M parameters, whereas LoRA requires only 4.7M parameters (a reduction of approximately 99.997% in trainable parameters) or 37.7M parameters (a reduction of approximately 99.978%). Despite this massive reduction, LoRA performs on-par with or better than Full Fine-tuning and Adapter-based methods. For example, on MNLI, GPT-3 with LoRA (4.7M parameters) achieves 91.7% accuracy, outperforming Full Fine-tuning (89.5% accuracy with 175,255.8M parameters) and AdapterH (89.8% accuracy with 7.1M parameters).
